notes.content: The opening continues the definition of the empty figure as the least element of the figure family, followed by disjoint figures implying compatible figures. After “On a, par les axiomes:”, (1.13) claims an equivalence with disjointness of shadows, explained as empty intersection and compatibility between every element of one shadow and every element of the other. The prose restatement uses no common lieux and disjointness between lieux “au sens de l’atelier”. The final paragraph stresses the two relations on M and L. For set-theoretic ateliers it calls the relations on L trivial: two lieux are always compatible and are disjoint iff distinct. The final sentence begins a contrast about the set-theoretic, moderate case and continues off the page.
math_reading_decisions: Literal om(G) occurs twice and is not regularized to omb(G).
The possible canceled equals sign is retained uncertain; H’s canceled empty-set symbol is unsupported. The separate live equality is clear.
The displayed word compatible and the corrected prose disjoint are both preserved. Neither was rewritten to reconcile the mathematics.
The t crossbars leave both occurrences of tout live; barred m is an abbreviation, not an equality. Tjrs is present before the corrected compatibles.
